extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer-review researchers, meta-researchers, and policy makers interested in biomedical peer-review
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic evaluation of experimental interventions aimed at improving the biomedical peer-review process by measuring outcomes such as review quality, review duration, acceptance rates, manuscript quality, and error detection across randomized trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the peer-review process; reported as mean change in review quality and pooled across studies as standardized mean difference (SMD) based on the definitions used in the individual studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main outcome in 13 studies; reviewer-level interventions were associated with a significant improvement in review quality (network meta-analysis SMD 0.20 [0.06 to 0.33]). Note: individual studies used varying definitions of 'quality', so operationalization differs across trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of the peer-review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Time taken to complete peer review; differences between traditional and intervention-modified processes were pooled as SMD in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main outcome in 11 studies; reviewer-level interventions were associated with increased duration (SMD 0.15 [0.01 to 0.29]), indicating a trade-off between improved review quality and longer review times. Author- and editor-level interventions did not significantly impact duration (reported SMDs non-significant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance/rejection rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of interventions on the proportion of manuscripts accepted versus rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an outcome in 5 studies. Used to assess whether interventions alter editorial decision outcomes; no pooled estimate reported in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the manuscript itself after or as affected by the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an outcome in 4 studies. Used to evaluate whether peer-review interventions lead to measurable improvements in manuscript content or presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of errors detected
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of errors identified in manuscripts during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in 3 studies as an outcome; used as an objective metric of review thoroughness and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention level classification (author-, reviewer-, editor-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of interventions according to the level at which they act: author-level, reviewer-level, and editor-level (some studies investigated multiple levels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eight studies evaluated author-level, 16 reviewer-level, and 3 editor-level interventions. Reviewer-level modifications showed significant improvements in review quality (with increased duration), whereas author- and editor-level interventions did not significantly impact quality or duration in pooled analyses reported in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer blinding (specific reviewer-level intervention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Blinding reviewers to author identity (single/double/blind review approaches) evaluated as a reviewer-level intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Was a reviewer-level intervention examined across studies and is noted as an exception to the general trade-off: improvements associated with reviewer-level interventions occurred at the cost of increased duration 'except for reviewer blinding' (i.e., reviewer blinding did not increase duration in the same way).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized mean difference (SMD) as effect size
rubrics_metrics.description: Pooling metric: differences between traditional and intervention-modified peer-review processes were pooled as standardized mean difference (SMD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMD was used to synthesize heterogeneous definitions/measures across trials for outcomes such as review quality and duration. Interpret pooled SMDs with attention to study-level operational definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence design: randomized trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion criterion / quality standard: randomized trials comparing different peer-review interventions at author-, reviewer-, and/or editor-level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The systematic review included only randomized trials; 24 randomized trials were identified out of 575 retrieved studies. This emphasizes randomized experimental design as the preferred evidence standard for evaluating peer-review interventions.
